name: Scalp Acne
description: Scalp acne, also known as seborrheic dermatitis or dandruff, is a common skin condition that affects the scalp. It can manifest in various forms and may be accompanied by redness, itching, and flaky skin.
symptoms: Pimples and whiteheads on the scalp
risk_factors: Certain skin conditions like acne or eczema

daily_routine.purpose: Remove excess oil and dead skin cells without irritating the scalp.
Help reduce inflammation and control sebum production.
Nourish and moisturize the hair and scalp, but avoid applying it to the scalp directly.

lifestyle_tips: Avoid tight hairstyles and excessive heat styling
Regular scalp massages to stimulate blood circulation
common_myths: Scalp acne is caused by poor hygiene.
Using harsh shampoos will clear up scalp acne.
when_to_consult_doctor: If symptoms persist or worsen, if there is significant hair loss, or if you experience severe itching and discomfort.
prevention: Regularly clean your hair and scalp

severity_levels.mild: Mild scalp acne may present with minimal redness, mild itching, and occasional flakiness. Treatment often involves over-the-counter anti-dandruff shampoos.
severity_levels.moderate: Moderate scalp acne includes more frequent symptoms such as increased redness, persistent flakiness, and more visible dandruff or pimples on the scalp. Prescription-strength treatments may be necessary for effective management.
severity_levels.severe: Severe scalp acne can lead to significant hair loss, intense itching, and noticeable lesions on the scalp. Professional treatment is essential, including prescription medications and possibly phototherapy.

expert_tips: Consistency in using recommended products is key to managing scalp acne.
Avoid scratching or rubbing the scalp as it can irritate the skin further.
Consider consulting a dermatologist for personalized treatment plans.
